segments.text: On the back, Lucian had written, "I'm sorry I couldn't stay."
segments.vi: Ở mặt sau, Lucian đã viết: "Tôi xin lỗi vì đã không thể ở lại."

segments.text: Adrian closed his eyes.
For the first time since meeting Lucian, he was afraid.
Not of losing someone he loved, but of discovering that he had already lost him.
Three weeks had passed since Lucian disappeared.
Adrian still went to the flower shop every evening, even though the doors remained locked.
He had stopped calling Lucian's phone.
He had stopped asking people if they had seen him.
But he had not stopped waiting.
One rainy afternoon, Adrian returned to the shop
and noticed something beneath the counter that he had never seen before.
A small wooden box with his name carved into the lid.
Inside were dozens of envelopes.
Then dozens more.
Adrian counted them slowly.
There were 365 in total.
Each envelope had a date written on it.
His hands began to shake as he opened the first one.
Day one. The day I met you.
The letter was short.
Lucian wrote about the wrong bouquet, about Adrian's serious expression,
and about how strangely happy he had felt after making a stranger smile.
Adrian opened the next letter. Then another.
Each one described a day they had spent together.
Every coffee, every walk, every rainy evening, every small moment Adrian had forgotten
but Lucien had carefully remembered.
By the 10th letter, Adrian was crying.
By the hundredth, he could barely see the words.
Then he reached the letters marked with the final months.
They were different.
Lucien wrote less about their happy moments and more about time.
I went to the hospital today.
The doctor said there isn't much they can do anymore.
I didn't tell Adrian.
I don't want his last memories of me to be hospital rooms and medicine.
Adrian stopped breathing for a moment.
He read the sentence again. Then again.
Lucien had been sick all along.
The strange tiredness.
The hospital visits.
The days when he disappeared for hours.
The question about having one perfect year.
It all suddenly made sense.
Adrian pressed the letter against his chest and broke down.
"You idiot." he whispered.
"Why didn't you tell me?"
The next envelope contained a photograph of Lucien smiling at the camera.
On the back was a simple sentence.
If I tell him, he'll stay.
And if he stays, he'll watch me disappear.
Adrian opened another letter.
"I love him too much to make him spend his life remembering how I died."
That night, Adrian read every remaining letter until sunrise.
